```{r}
#| label: Install
#| include: false
### Utilities for R.

# Necessary packages
packages_required <- c(
  # R tools
  "knitr", "tidyverse", 
  # Scientific packages
  "ade4", "divent", "GoFKernel", "sads", "untb", "vegan"
)
# Already installed?
packages_installed <- vapply(
  packages_required, 
  FUN = requireNamespace, 
  FUN.VALUE = TRUE, 
  quietly = TRUE
) 
# Install missing packages
install.packages(names(packages_installed)[!packages_installed])

# Chunk font size hook: allows size='small' 
# or any valid Latex font size in chunk options
def.chunk.hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("chunk")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(
  chunk = function(x, options) {
    x <- def.chunk.hook(x, options)
    ifelse(
      options$size == "normalsize", 
      yes = x,
      no = paste0("\n \\", options$size, "\n\n", x, "\n\n \\normalsize")
    )
  }
)
```

# Species distributions

## Figures

Explication of data: 50 (representing 50 ha) rows and 225 species (columns)

Exploring the data with different representations; histogram with a log axis and line density plot with normal axes.

### Preston diagram

```{r}
library("tidyverse")
library("vegan")
data(BCI)
# Sum the 50 1-ha plots
BCI_50ha_abd <- colSums(BCI) #all trees in BCI
BCI_50ha_abd/50 #trees per hectar (in Paracou there is 600 per ha)
BCI_50ha_abd %>% # BCI contains this number of trees per plot
  #need to put it in a log scale in order to see the real distibution. If not, we loose the view on the rare species because around 50 species will take up most of the space
  log10() %>% #log scale representation 0 is 1 (log1=0), 2 is 100, 3 is 1000
  hist(breaks = 15, main = "Preston diagram") #gives 16 bars - 15 breaks between them, without defined breaks the histogram is automaticaly created that might not be very precise
```

Probability densities

```{r}
BCI_50ha_abd %>% 
  tibble(abundance = .) %>% #ggplot cannot work with vectors so it needs to be transformed into a tibble so i have only the numbers
  ggplot() + 
  # Bounded density - bounds means that the density is bounded - there are no possible values below 0 
  geom_density(aes(x = abundance), bounds = c(0, Inf)) +
  scale_x_log10()
```

2 very abundant species

```{r}
max(BCI_50ha_abd) #to see the species with the highest density
```

## Broken stick

Random distributions are created by `divent::rxxx()`functions.

Rxxx to draw random distribution

```{r}
rcommunity(
  # One community
  1,
  # Number of trees
  size = 10000,
  # Number of species
  species_number = 300,
  # Distribution
  distribution = "bstick"
) %>% 
  # Whittaker plot
  autoplot()
```

## Geometric

It is very uneven.
Large numbers of individuals are needed.
Only used for example for soil microbes to describe their distribution.

Microbes live in a very competitive system where the first species have a very unequal chance to occupy spaces.
There is a real "first comes first serves" idea in communities creating a very strong hierarchy in the system.

A sequential broken stick.

Random distribution.

```{r}
rcommunity(
  # One community - in this model the number of species is what defined and what % of the resources the first species will get
  1,
  # Number of trees
  size = 1E6,#10000 original number
  # Number of species
  species_number = 300,
  # Distribution
  distribution = "geom", #geometric distribution
  prob_geom = 0.1
) %>% 
  # Whittaker plot
  autoplot()
```

## Estimate the parameters

Draw a very large lognormal distribution.

```{r}
rcommunity(
  # One community
  1,
  # Number of trees = max supported integer value
  size = .Machine$integer.max, #Machine is a number of variables created by r
  # Number of species
  species_number = 300,
  # Distribution
  distribution = "lnorm",
  sd_lnorm = 1 #data is simulated with sigma = 1
) %>% 
  # Name it
  mutate(site = "Large log-normal") ->
  comm_large_lnorm
# Plot it
comm_large_lnorm %>% 
  autoplot()
```

Sample it.

```{r}
# Draw 3000 trees from the large community
rcommunity(
  1,
  size = 3000,
  abd = as.numeric(comm_large_lnorm) #abundance argument 
) %>% 
  # Name it
  mutate(site = "Small log-normal") ->
  comm_small_lnorm
# Make a single tibble with all data
comm_large_lnorm %>% 
  # Make a single tibble
  bind_rows(comm_small_lnorm) -> #binding two tibbles - I think they need to be the same size
  comm_lnorm
# Plot the distributions and fit a lognormal model
autoplot(comm_lnorm, fit_rac = TRUE, distribution = "lnorm")
#there is a fitted line of lognormal distribution
# Estimate the parameters
fit_rac(comm_lnorm, distribution = "lnorm") 
```

Fit the distrinbution of BCI:

```{r}
BCI_50ha_abd %>% 
  as_abundances() %>% 
  autoplot(fit_rac = TRUE, distribution = "lnorm") #fitting other models: "geom",  "bstick"for broken stick distibution, logseries "lseries" 
```

## Zero-sum multinomial distribution

A hard way to simulate a distribution that fits neutral model.

BCI parameters $\theta$ and $m$ are estimated following @etienne2005 with the *untb* package.

Here is the code to run it with the BCA data.
Already loaded is a file.
The data is too large for R to compute it.
R does not have enough integer space to compute it.

```{r}
#| label: bci_params
#| echo: true
# BCI data
library("vegan")
data(BCI)
BCI_50ha <- colSums(BCI)
# Don't load untb because of conflicts with dplyr::count() and select()
# library("untb")
if (file.exists("data/BCI_logkda.RData")) {
  # Use the saved result if available to save
  # computation resources
  load("data/BCI_logkda.RData")
} else {
  BCI_50ha %>% 
  # name conflict with dplyr::count()
  untb::count() %>% 
  # requires pari/gp installed and in the search paths,
  # or use gp_binary argument
  untb::logkda() ->
  BCI_logkda
  # Save the result
  save(BCI_logkda, file = "data/BCI_logkda.RData")
}
BCI_50ha %>% 
  # name conflict with dplyr::count()
  untb::count() %>% 
  # Estimate theta and m
  untb::optimal.params(log.kda = BCI_logkda) %>% 
  print() ->
  BCI_params
```

#Theta 47 means that in a metacommunity 47 slope, fundamental number of biodiversity in metacommunity, fishers alpha is theta in the metacommunity - to send migrants to the community.
Migration is approx.
0.1 so 10% - the migration always depends on theta.

The distribution of the local community is derived.
$J$ is that of BCI and $m$ was estimated previously.

#Simulation of BCI data with the neutral model.
After compare with real data.

```{r}
#| label: bci_sim_code
#| echo: true
J <- sum(BCI) #size of the community
theta <- BCI_params[1] #metacommunity descriptor
m <- BCI_params[2] #migration factor
library("sads")
# Number of species in the local community
Svolkov(theta, m, J) %>% 
  # Must be integers for the simulation
  round() %>% 
  # Draw the species abundances
  rvolkov(theta, m, J) %>%  #theta belongs to metacommunity, m and Jis a parameter of community, not metacommunity. J is the size of the community
  # Make it an abundances object top plot it
  as_abundances() %>% 
  # Whittaker plot
  autoplot() ->
  BCI_sim_neutral
# BCI real distribution
BCI_50ha %>% #get the real data
  sort(decreasing = TRUE) %>%  #sorting from the most to the least abundant
  as_tibble() %>% #making a tibble by rank
  mutate(rank = seq_len(n())) -> #rank computing
  BCI_tbl_50ha #the created data
# Plot altogether
BCI_sim_neutral +
  geom_line( #adding a line that is the real data of BCI - herethe simulation and then add the real data added on it
    data = BCI_tbl_50ha,
    aes(x = rank, y = value)
  )
```

# Species Accumulation Curves

## BCI data

Gather all subplots.

```{r}
library("vegan")
data(BCI)
BCI %>% 
  # Make an abundances object
  as_abundances() %>% 
  # Make all plot weights equals
  mutate(weight = 1) %>% 
  # Gather all 50 plots
  metacommunity() %>% 
  # Name it
  mutate(site = "BCI") -> 
  BCI_all #all distribution of 50 plots of BCI
autoplot(BCI_all, fit_rac = TRUE, distribution = "lnorm")
fit_rac(BCI_all, distribution = "lnorm") 
```

Abundance frequency counts help read the figure.

```{r}
BCI %>% 
colSums() %>% 
abd_freq_count() %>% 
arrange(desc(abundance))
```

## Accumulation of subplots

Accumulate subplots in random order (Monte-Carlo).
Plot the expectation and the confidence interval of the number of species with respect to the number of samples.

```{r}
BCI %>% #accumulation curve row by row (where the columns are species) avarage
  specaccum() %>% #accumulation of subplots(a function of vegan)
  plot()
```

## Accumulation curve

Compute the expected accumulation curve of BCI up to twice the sampling effort, with its confidence interval.

#Species accumulation curve - depends a lot on a sampling size - exact sampling effort.
If it is small adding a few species can have a big effect.
You need to have large samples.
It gets relatively flat at 10000 samples (when it starts to be relatively flat)

```{r}
#in respect to a certain number of trees
#but what about area?

# Number of trees in BCI
BCI_n <- abd_sum(BCI_all, as_numeric = TRUE) #counting the number of trees
# Asymptotic richness
BCI_richness <- div_richness(BCI_all, as_numeric = TRUE) #how many species are there in total
BCI_all %>% 
  accum_hill(
    levels = seq(from = 1, to = 2 * BCI_n, by = 10), #up to 2x the size of sample, extrapolation is valable (according to Caho 2014) by= calculation of every 10
    # Run simulations to estimate uncertainty.
    # Start with 10 simulations, run 100 later
    n_simulations = 10, #multinomial simulation
  ) %>% 
  autoplot() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = BCI_n, linetype = 2) + #creating a vetical line on the plot (here we set it to the sample size - after it is extrapolated)
  geom_hline(yintercept = BCI_richness, linetype = 1)
#only ten times simulated - in order to get a better confidence line you would need 1000 times
#confidence interval gets narrower because there are less to miss because the model because the model is in the rare species area
```

# Canonical lognormal

ggplot seems to bug with weighted, bounded density and log scale.

```{r}
# Most adundant species
BCI_50ha_mas <- max(BCI_50ha_abd)
BCI_50ha_abd %>% 
  tibble(abundance = .) %>% 
  ggplot() +
  # Bounded density
  geom_density(
    aes(x = abundance, color = "Species curve"), 
    bounds = c(0, Inf)
  ) +
  # Weighted density
  geom_density(
    aes(x = abundance, weight = abundance, color = "Individuals curve"), 
    bounds = c(min(BCI_50ha_abd), max(BCI_50ha_abd))
  ) +
  scale_x_log10()
```

Correct curves.

```{r}
library("GoFKernel")
plot(
  density.reflected(log10(BCI_50ha_abd), lower = 0),
  type = "l", 
  col = "red", 
  ylim = c(0, .8),
  main = "Canonical BCI",
  xlab = "log10(abundance)"
)
lines(
  density.reflected(
    log10(BCI_50ha_abd), 
    weights = BCI_50ha_abd, 
    lower = min(log10(BCI_50ha_abd)), 
    upper = max(log10(BCI_50ha_abd))
  )
)
abline(v = max(log10(BCI_50ha_abd)), lty = 2)

```

The red curve is the smoothed Preston plot of BCI, i.e. the probability density for a species to contain a given number of individuals.
The black curve is the probability for an individual to belong to a species that contains that number of individuals.
If it reaches its maximum value for the most abundant species, then the lognormal distribution is canonical.

(# the red line is representing the most abundant species. The mean of the most abundant speceis which is here shown as half of the normal distibution.check)

Estimators of richness.

```{r}
div_richness(p6_abundances, estimator = "naive") %>%
```

## Interpolation / extrapolation

Diversity of 1 ha in Paracou.
Accumulation curve is obtained by rarification.

```{r}
# Number of trees per hectare - to get the number for standardisation

  div_richness(level = round(p6_density)) #level is injected here for rarification
```

How to deal with calculations?

either calculate syptotic diversities for both (with Chao or Jack) but sometimes it is not possible to use - fx size is too small

small or large to use as standard?

# Shannon

Quantify the complexity.
The number of possible states.

## Information function

Information brought by an individual: $I(p_s) = \ln(1 / p_s)$.

```{r}
ggplot() +
  # Increase the default number of points (101 to 1001) for precision
  geom_function(fun = \(p) {log(1 / p)}, n = 1001) +
  labs(x = "Probability", y = "Information")
```

with 1 probability information - or surprise is very low

Information brought by a species: $p_s \ln(1 / p_s)$.

```{r}
# the surprise of seeing the rare tree only once is actually not that surprising - bringing in the concept of finding more of the same species - if we find more of them - we are more and more suprised
# ps time logged the 
# the weighted information plot where the numbers of species are considered 
#its a summed information - weithted information
ggplot() +
  geom_function(fun = \(p) {p * log(1 / p)}, n = 1001) +
  labs(x = "Probability", y = "Information")
```

## Paracou 6

Estimators.

Shannon entropy estimators

The three different types - H is entropy - entropy is estimated and used to calculate unseen diversity

```{r}
ent_shannon(p6_abundances, estimator = "naive") %>% 
  bind_rows(ent_shannon(p6_abundances, estimator = "UnveilJ")) %>% 
  bind_rows(ent_shannon(p6_abundances, estimator = "ChaoJost")) %>% 
  print() ->
  p6_shannon 
#weight is the same for all - because they are standardized on the size
```

H is difficult to interpret - put into numbers - effective number of species

Calculate the diversity - effective number

Effective number of species: $e^H$.

```{r}
p6_shannon %>% 
  mutate(diversity = exp(entropy))
```

101 or 110 species - species per plot

Unveiled distribution.

```{r}
p6_abundances %>% 
  # Unveil the species probabilities
  probabilities(estimator = "Chao2015", unveiling = "geometric") %>% 
  # Rename the distribution to recognize it
  mutate(site = "Unveiled probabilities") %>% 
  # Add the naive probability estimators
  bind_rows(
    p6_abundances %>% 
      # Just divide n_s by n
      probabilities() %>% 
      # Rename the distribution to recognize it
      mutate(site = "Naive probabilities")
  ) %>% 
  autoplot() +
  labs(color = "Estimation")
```

# Simpson

## Paracou 6

Estimators.

```{r}
ent_simpson(p6_abundances, estimator = "naive") %>% 
  bind_rows(ent_simpson(p6_abundances, estimator = "Lande")) %>% 
  bind_rows(ent_simpson(p6_abundances, estimator = "UnveilJ")) %>% 
  bind_rows(ent_simpson(p6_abundances, estimator = "ChaoJost")) %>% 
  print() ->
  p6_simpson
```

Effective number of species: $1 / (1 - E)$.

```{r}
p6_simpson %>% 
  mutate(diversity = 1 / (1 - entropy))
```

# Generalized entropy

## Information

Information brought by an individual: $I(p_s) = \ln_q(1 / p_s)$.

```{r}
ggplot() +
  # Increase the default number of points (101 to 1001) for precision
  geom_function(fun = \(p) {ln_q(1 / p, q = 0)}, n = 1001, aes(color = "0")) + 
  geom_function(fun = \(p) {ln_q(1 / p, q = 1)}, n = 1001, aes(color = "1")) + 
  geom_function(fun = \(p) {ln_q(1 / p, q = 2)}, n = 1001, aes(color = "2")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 10)) +
  labs(x = "Probability", y = "Information", color = "q")
```

Information brought by a species: $p_s \ln_q(1 / p_s)$.

```{r}
ggplot() +
  # Increase the default number of points (101 to 1001) for precision
  geom_function(fun = \(p) {p * ln_q(1 / p, q = 0)}, n = 1001, aes(color = "0")) + 
  geom_function(fun = \(p) {p * ln_q(1 / p, q = 1)}, n = 1001, aes(color = "1")) + 
  geom_function(fun = \(p) {p * ln_q(1 / p, q = 2)}, n = 1001, aes(color = "2")) +
  labs(x = "Probability", y = "Information", color  = "q")
```

## Paracou 6

Diversity profile.

With profile_hill calculate the diversity profile

Hill number - diversity number

```{r}
p6_abundances %>% 
  profile_hill() %>% 
  autoplot() +
  # Don't print the legend
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Compare estimators.

```{r}
p6_abundances %>% 
  profile_hill(estimator = "UnveilJ") %>%
  # Use the site name to store the estimator's name
  mutate(site = "UnveilJ") %>% 
  bind_rows(
    p6_abundances %>% 
    profile_hill(estimator = "ChaoJost") %>% 
    mutate(site = "ChaoJost")
  ) %>% 
  bind_rows(
    p6_abundances %>% 
    profile_hill(estimator = "naive") %>% 
    mutate(site = "naive")
  ) %>% 
  autoplot() +
  labs(color  = "Estimator")
```

Extreme values.

The reciprocal of the Berger-Parker index [@Berger1970] is the rarity of the most abundant species $^{+\infty}D$.

```{r}
# q = 1000 is enough for infinity
div_hill(p6_abundances, q = 1000)
# Compare to 
p6_abundances %>% 
  # Extract proobabilities
  as_probabilities(as_numeric = TRUE) %>% 
  # Max value
  max() %>% 
  # Reciprocal
  `^`(-1)
  
```

# Comparing diversity

## Asymptotic diversity

Compare asymptotic diversity of Paracou and BCI, extend $q$.

```{r}
# Orders from 0 to 4
q_seq_0_4 <- seq(from = 0, to = 4, by = 0.1)
profile_hill(p6_abundances, orders = q_seq_0_4) %>% 
  bind_rows(profile_hill(BCI_all, orders = q_seq_0_4)) %>% 
  autoplot()
```

## Standardized diversity

The sampling effort is very different: 50 ha in BCI, 6.25 ha in Paracou.
- standardizing on a chosen area size The asymptotic estimation is less reliable in Paracou.

Compare diversity at the same sampling effort, say 10 ha.

```{r}
# Number of trees in 10 ha
p6_n_10ha <- round(abd_sum(p6_abundances, as_numeric = TRUE) / 6.25 * 10)
BCI_n_10_ha <- round(sum(BCI_all) / 5)
```

Compare diversity of 10 ha.

```{r}
profile_hill(p6_abundances, level = p6_n_10ha) %>% 
  bind_rows(profile_hill(BCI_all, level = BCI_n_10_ha)) %>% 
  autoplot()
```

## Sample coverage

```{r}
coverage(p6_abundances) %>% 
  bind_rows(coverage(BCI_all))
```

Compare diversity at the same sample coverage [@Chao2012b], that of Paracou.

```{r}
reference_coverage <- coverage(p6_abundances, as_numeric = TRUE)
profile_hill(p6_abundances, level = reference_coverage) %>% 
  bind_rows(profile_hill(BCI_all, level = reference_coverage)) %>% 
  autoplot()
```


Rao.

```{r}
ent_rao(mock_3sp_abundances, tree = mock_3sp_tree, estimator = "naive")
```

The tree is normalized to height = 1 by default.
Without normalization:

```{r}
ent_rao(
  mock_3sp_abundances, 
  tree = mock_3sp_tree, 
  estimator = "naive", 
  normalize = FALSE
)
```

## Paracou 6

`paracou_6_taxo` is a taxonomic tree: distance is 1 between species of the same genus, 2 between genera of the same family, 3 between families.

```{r}
plot(paracou_6_taxo, type = "fan", show.tip.label = FALSE) 
```

Calculate Rao's entropy and phylogenetic entropy of order 2

```{r}
ent_rao(p6_abundances, tree = paracou_6_taxo) %>% 
  bind_rows(
    ent_phylo(p6_abundances, tree = paracou_6_taxo, q = 2)
  )
```

Rao's entropy is not an effective number of species, but the average phylogenetic distance between two individuals.
The corresponding Hill number is:

```{r}
div_phylo(p6_abundances, tree = paracou_6_taxo, q = 2)
```

Diversity profile

```{r}
profile_phylo(p6_abundances, tree = paracou_6_taxo) %>% 
  autoplot()
```

# Functional diversity

## Mock data

The same mock data is used.
Distances between species is now assumed to be in the trait space.
Distances between species.

```{r}
mock_3sp_dist
```

```{r}
library("ade4")
mock_pcoa <- dudi.pco(mock_3sp_dist, scannf = FALSE)
```

Similarity between species.

```{r}
# The dist object must be converted to a matrix
mock_3sp_Z <- 1 - as.matrix(mock_3sp_dist) / max(mock_3sp_dist)
mock_3sp_Z
```

Ordinariness.

```{r}
# Probabilities of species
mock_3sp_prob <- mock_3sp_abd / sum(mock_3sp_abd)
# Ordinariness of species
mock_3sp_O <- as.numeric(mock_3sp_Z %*% mock_3sp_prob)
# Compare probabilities and ordinariness
tibble(
  Probability = mock_3sp_prob,
  Rarity_p = 1 / mock_3sp_prob,
  Ordinariness = mock_3sp_O,
  Rarity_0 = 1 / mock_3sp_O
)
```

Diversity.

```{r}
profile_similarity(
  mock_3sp_abundances, 
  similarities = mock_3sp_Z,

```

Diversity of order 2 (i.e. Rao's).

```{r}
ent_similarity(
  mock_3sp_abundances, 
  similarities = mock_3sp_Z, 
  q = 2, 
  estimator = "naive"
)
```

## Intraspecific variability

Coordinates of species A, B and C in the trait space.

```{r}
mock_pcoa$li
```

Plot individuals in the trait space, with a small variability.

```{r}
# Create coordinates
tibble(
  Species = rep(names(mock_3sp_abd), times = mock_3sp_abd),
  x = rep(mock_pcoa$li[, 1], times = mock_3sp_abd),
  y = rep(mock_pcoa$li[, 2], times = mock_3sp_abd)
) ->
  mock_3sp_ind
# Choose variability
variability <- 0.1
# Map
mock_3sp_ind %>% 
  # Add variability
  mutate(
    x = x + rnorm(n(), mean = 0, sd = variability),
    y = y + rnorm(n(), mean = 0, sd = variability)
  ) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, color = Species)) +
  geom_point() +
  coord_fixed()
```

Diversity of the 6 individuals.
First, without variability.

```{r}
# Choose variability
variability <- 0
# Create the point set
mock_3sp_ind %>% 
  # Add variability
  mutate(
    x = x + rnorm(n(), mean = 0, sd = variability),
    y = y + rnorm(n(), mean = 0, sd = variability)
  )  %>% 
  # Distance matrix
  dist() %>% 
  as.matrix() ->
  mock_6ind_dist
# Delete the row and column name of the matrix (they are not species names)
rownames(mock_6ind_dist) <- colnames(mock_6ind_dist) <- NULL
# Total abundance
mock_6ind_n <- nrow(mock_6ind_dist)
# Similarity
mock_6ind_Z <- 1 - mock_6ind_dist / max(mock_6ind_dist)
# Abundances of individuals are 1, or any identical value
mock_6ind_abd <- rep(1, mock_6ind_n)
# Diversity
profile_similarity(
  mock_6ind_abd, 
  similarities = mock_6ind_Z,
  estimator = "naive"
) %>% 
  autoplot()
```

Change the variability (0.1 first) and run the code again.

# Diversity partitioning

## Mock data

Three habitats: A, B, C.

```{r}
matrix( #original with numbers of 1 - 1 single of species
  c(
    0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3,
    3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 0, 3, 0, 0,
    0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 3, 3, 3
  ),
  nrow = 3, 
  byrow = TRUE
) %>% 
  as_abundances() %>% 
  mutate(
    site = paste("Habitat", LETTERS[1:3]),
    weight = 1
  ) ->
  mock_island_abd
```

Richness.

```{r}
div_richness(mock_island_abd)
div_richness(mock_island_abd, gamma = TRUE) #for metacommunity all the species that can be found at least once in any of the 3 habitats
```

Multiplicative partitioning: 10 effective species ($\gamma$) = 5 effective species per habitat ($\alpha$) times 2 habitats ($\beta$).

Because of the naive estimator does not work - we need to remove it

```{r}
#div_part(mock_island_abd, q = 0, estimator = "naive")
```

```{r}
div_part(mock_island_abd, q = 0)
```

Alpha is diversity in communities (number of species)

beta is gamma/alpha

gamma metacommunity - all

Additive partitioning: 10 effective species ($\gamma$) = 5 effective species per habitat ($\alpha$) + 5 more species ($\beta$).

## Paracou 6

The plot is made of 4 subplots.

```{r}
# Diversity profiles of the 4 subplots
paracou_6_abd %>% 
  profile_hill() %>% 
  autoplot()
```

### Partitioning

Function `div_part()` computes $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ diversity.

```{r}
div_part(paracou_6_abd, q = 1)
```

### Step by step

```{r}
# Alpha entropy
paracou_6_abd %>% 
  ent_tsallis(q = 1) %>% 
  # Mean entropy
  group_by(order) %>% 
  summarise(ent_alpha = mean(entropy)) %>% 
  # Diversity
  mutate(div_alpha = exp_q(ent_alpha, q = 1)) %>% 
  print() ->
  paracou_6_alpha
```

check the q number!

```{r}
# Gamma entropy
paracou_6_abd %>% 
  # Group the subplots
  metacommunity() %>% 
  ent_tsallis(q = 1) %>%
  # Rename entropy for clarity
  rename(ent_gamma = entropy) %>% 
  # Diversity
  mutate(div_gamma = exp_q(ent_gamma, q = 1)) %>% 
  print() ->
  paracou_6_gamma
```

```{r}
# Make a single tibble with alpha and gamma diversities
paracou_6_alpha %>% 
  bind_cols(
    paracou_6_gamma %>% 
      select(ent_gamma, div_gamma)
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    # beta entropy
    ent_beta = ent_gamma - ent_alpha,
    # beta diversity
    div_beta = div_gamma / div_alpha
  )
```

### Profiles

Not implemented yet in divent.

alpha diversity.

```{r}
# Values of q used for computation: default values of profile_xxx()
orders <- seq(from = 0, to = 2, by = 0.1)
sapply(
  # Apply ent_tsallis to all orders
  orders,
  FUN = \(q) {
    # Get a number to obtain a matrix with sapply
    ent_tsallis(paracou_6_abd, q = q, as_numeric = TRUE)
  }
) %>% 
  # Each row contains a subbplot, each column an order, values are entropy
  # Calculate mean entropy (weights are equal)
  colMeans() %>% 
  # Diversity
  exp_q(q = orders) %>% 
  # Make a tibble
  tibble(
    order = orders,
    div_alpha = .
  ) %>% 
  print() ->
  paracou_6_alpha_profile
```

gamma diversity.

```{r}
paracou_6_abd %>% 
  profile_hill(gamma = TRUE) %>% 
  # Rename diversity to recongnize gamma later
  rename(div_gamma = diversity) %>% 
  print() ->
  paracou_6_gamma_profile
```

Compute beta.

```{r}
paracou_6_gamma_profile %>% 
  # Join the tibbles by identical order
  inner_join(paracou_6_alpha_profile) %>% 
  # Calculate beta diversity
  mutate(div_beta = div_gamma / div_alpha) %>% 
  print() ->
  paracou_6_profile
```

Plot.

```{r}
paracou_6_profile %>% 
  # paracou_6_profile is an object of class profile that can be plotted
  # The column to plot must be named diversity
  rename(diversity = div_alpha) %>% 
  autoplot() + 
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r}
paracou_6_profile %>% 
  # rename div_beta to plot it
  rename(diversity = div_beta) %>% 
  autoplot() + 
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
